metadata.notes: Baseline for sift-email using Gmail's Important mark and star, a time-based search for new mail, and a daily review of how the user handles mail (PR #129, issue #128), evals 1-25, two runs each, with run-mcp-trials.sh against the Gmail, Claude Docs, and Contacts stubs. Both runs were on SKILL.md as of commit 8783315, run in parallel with separate trial directories under $TMPDIR. Every eval prompt starts with /sift-email. Both runs were on 2026-10-24 in the rubric timezone (2026-10-25 in UTC for eval 1, whose starter rubric is UTC); fixtures are anchored to 2026-10-10 and shifted two weeks by fixture-dates.py, and graders held the run date to the date the run's clock gave. Failures: eval 5 run 1 (the (observed) rule named the sender but not the Low priority it applies), eval 7 run 1 (starred the landlord thread again after the user had removed sift's star, because the new message asked something), and eval 11 run 2 (read the whole rubric before the Step 2 checks, as in the previous baseline). Not graded: eval 11 run 1 rewrote the empty run's heading as a plain paragraph, which the next run's search reads its start from; eval 13 run 2 stored an account's last four digits in an (inferred) About me note; eval 2 run 1 marked a 'Got it, thanks!' reply Important under the 90-day rule though its searches found no mail to that sender; the Bulk and Junk split for marketing mail varies between runs (eval 1's promo, eval 21's sale); run headings sometimes land at the wrong level or above the Runs intro; the Daily review note usually sits in the run summary rather than on its own line; and unrequested (inferred) About me notes and category labels.
